ranking.note: Raised to P1 and moved up six places: data integrity is this category's first criterion, and a node continuing to run after corrupt index/coin reads (corruption masked as absent keys) is the clearest category-critical hazard here.

Raised to P1: fixes a reindex startup race and a reorg stale-query window and is the prerequisite for the out-of-process index project (#10102) and shared chain-sync (#15719), i.e. it blocks a category-defining effort.

Moved up five places: iterator failures reported as 'transaction not found' is a silent wrong-answer bug, which outranks sync-time and feature work in this category; kept at P2 because it is a narrow follow-up to the broader #34132 policy.
Placed ahead of #26966 because it extracts the batching foundation that the parallel-sync PR builds on; reviewing it first unblocks the larger speedup.

Placed below the integrity and sync-performance work: new index types with a stated consumer rank last among the category's substantive concerns, though the Electrum/explorer demand keeps it firmly P2.
Lowered to P4: a one-shot deletion of an obsolete directory is narrow housekeeping, clearly below the architectural cleanup of #35474 which it was sharing a band with.

inconsistencies: #34132 and #36789 address the same failure mode in txindex reads (errors masked as 'not found'). #34132 sets the broader policy (fatal abort via CDBWrapper) and may subsume or conflict with #36789's dbwrapper_error throw; decide #34132's approach first, then rebase or close #36789 accordingly.
Chain: #34489 (batched index writes) is explicitly the extracted foundation for #26966 (parallel index sync), and #34489 itself depends on merged #34897. Review order must be #34489 then #26966.

#24230 and #35474 both restructure how indexes are owned and reached (interfaces/NodeContext vs process globals). They will collide across RPC/REST/net_processing call sites; settle #24230's decoupling direction first so #35474 does not re-plumb ownership in a way that has to be redone.

#36480 prepares txospenderindex for pruned mode using block sequence numbers, while #36002 implements pruned mode for txindex using the same compact-key/sequence scheme (from merged #35531). Reviewing #36002 first fixes the pruned-lookup semantics (missing-block-hash surfacing) that #36480 will inherit.
result.notes: The list splits cleanly along the category's stated order: data-integrity/correctness (#34132, #24230, #36789), then user-facing capability and sync/resource cost (#36002, #34489, #26966, #36480), then a new index type with a named consumer (#36629), then internal tidying (#35474, #36292). Several PRs cluster in P2 because they are genuinely comparable in consequence, not for lack of differentiation.
